input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Paragraph (h) gives AP the affiliate/successor carve-out we require: it may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. The termination provisions (p0016) contain no change-of-control trigger and no re-pricing right for Kubient on AP's change of control, so the walk-away scenarios are absent. The clause is mutual rather than one-way, so it sits at the playbook fallback (mutual right to assign to successors, consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld); the only shortfalls of the preferred position are minor sub-elements — no express bar on assignment to an AP competitor and no written-notice mechanic — which we note but do not redline.
